instruction: Format this essay with the following spacing requirements: introduction with one-and-a-half spacing, body with double spacing, and conclusion with single spacing.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires setting line spacing for 3 paragraphs: paragraph 0 = 1.5, paragraph 1 = 2.0, paragraph 2 = 1.0. Evaluator checks each paragraph with tolerance of 0.01. Verified with document structure: 3 paragraphs present in source file. Partial credit: 0.33 per paragraph.

llm_judge_reasons: Semantic mismatch: Instruction refers to essay SECTIONS (introduction, body, conclusion) but evaluator checks individual PARAGRAPHS (para0, para1, para2)
Incorrect assumption: Essays typically have multiple paragraphs per section, but evaluator assumes each section is exactly one paragraph
Incomplete verification: If document has more than 3 paragraphs, evaluator only checks first 3 and ignores all others
Missing section identification logic: No mechanism to identify which paragraphs belong to introduction/body/conclusion sections
Logic flaw: User could correctly format paragraphs 0-2 but leave remaining essay paragraphs with wrong spacing and still get perfect score
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Either simplify instruction to match evaluator: 'Set spacing for first 3 paragraphs: para 0=1.5, para 1=2.0, para 2=1.0' (removes ambiguity about sections)

Or enhance evaluator to handle multi-paragraph sections: Add logic to identify section boundaries (e.g., via paragraph styles, headings, or manual paragraph ranges) and verify ALL paragraphs in each section
Verify actual document structure: Check if the source document actually has only 3 paragraphs matching intro/body/conclusion, or if it has more paragraphs that need verification
Add comprehensive coverage: Evaluator should check ALL paragraphs in document, not just first 3, to ensure complete task verification
